title: Do not listen to the voice of despair.
body:
Discouragement often speaks to our hearts as if it were the truth. When we struggle with sin, experience pain in relationships, grow weary of family, or encounter failure, we may feel as though God has forgotten us. But the voice of discouragement is not the voice of truth.

Every day in our lives is not a coincidence to God, for before we were born, He already knew our days and held the story of our lives with His wisdom and grace, and even the unexpected hardships did not ever surprise God.

Believers do not write their own stories alone. Our Savior, the Lord, is the One who helps us. He is the One who owns everything. He knows what is best and accomplishes it according to His will.

Therefore, when discouragement comes to shake our hearts, let us not look only at the situation before us, but let us look to God who possesses our lives. Our future is not in the hands of fear, but in the hands of the faithful God.

Our heavenly Father, who holds all things in your hands, I praise you because you know every day of my life and lead me with your wisdom and goodness. Please forgive me when I listen to the voice of despair more than your promises.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who died and rose from the dead, to give me a firm hope. May the Holy Spirit open my eyes to see His goodness today, and may I live by the hope of the good news, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Looking Through the Creation to the Creator
body:
This world is full of good things that God has given us. Food, homes, nature, possessions, relationships, and success are all gifts from God who is good. The problem is not with these gifts, but with our hearts.

We often love the gifts more than the Giver of those gifts. When life is comfortable and abundant, we may forget God and try to find satisfaction, security, and meaning in the things He has created. This is idolatrous worship that has gone astray.

God did not give the beauty of this world to replace Him, but to lead our hearts to God, the source of all life and goodness.

In Jesus Christ, grace opens our eyes again, so we do not stop at the minor glory of created things, but learn to see the majesty of God, the only One who can truly satisfy our hearts.

Our Father, full of glory, I praise you, because you have created all things and given me many good things. Please forgive me when I love the gift more than you, and seek satisfaction from the things you have created instead of God.

I thank Jesus Christ, who has led me back to true worship. May the Holy Spirit guard my heart, using the good things of this world with gratitude, and may they lead me to praise Him even more. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ, Amen.

title: Jesus Paid the Debt of All Sins
body:
We often think that we must be good enough to receive love, acceptance, or intimacy from God. We may feel that we need to prove ourselves worthy before we can approach Him. But this kind of thinking is not the gospel before God. No one can atone for their own sin. The law is not a receipt that tells us we are righteous, but a mirror that shows us that we are sinners who desperately need grace.

But Jesus Christ has completely cleansed our sins on the cross. He did not merely cover our sins temporarily, but bore our sins in reality. Therefore, those who are in Christ have no remaining debt of sin before God.

So we do not have to hide because of fear when we sin. We do not have to be hopeless or pretend nothing has happened, but we can come to Jesus, the One who has forgiven our sins, and receive mercy from Him.

Dear heavenly Father, who is just and full of mercy, I praise you because you have completely forgiven my sins in Jesus Christ. Please forgive me when I try to earn your love by my actions, or hide from you in fear when I sin.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who bore our sins on the cross. May the Holy Spirit make us confident in the good news, live by faith, humble ourselves, and pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: God who is not weak is our strength.
body:
Life in a world fallen into sin can easily exhaust us. Struggling with sin, taking care of family, loving and forgiving others, and being responsible each day all weaken our hearts and bodies. Sometimes, even living the Christian life seems difficult and burdensome.

But our hope is in God who never grows weary. The Scripture teaches that our help comes from the Lord, the Creator of heaven and earth. He does not grow tired or fall asleep, but He watches over His people at all times.

We are weak and easily tired, but God is never weary. We need rest, but His care never ceases. He upholds all His people, from now until eternity.

Therefore, when we are weary, do not try to squeeze more strength from ourselves, but rather run to God, our Keeper, who never slumbers, and Jesus Christ, our Savior, who is our strength today.

Father, who never slumbers or sleeps, I praise you because you always watch over and sustain your children. Please forgive me when I am tired and try to rely on my own strength more than on you.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who keeps me in His favor. May the Holy Spirit revive my spirit and help me to trust in God who never falters, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Weakness Opens the Way for Us to See God's Favor
body:
The biggest problem we face is not our weakness, but our deception that we are strong enough. We don't want to admit that we are weak, we don't want others to see that we need help, and we often pretend that we can manage our lives on our own.

But God did not create us to live without relying on Him. We were created to rely on God, and in Jesus Christ, we are brought back to life through His grace. God does not take pleasure in seeing our weakness.

The gospel is the story of the strong Savior who gives grace and strength to the weak. Sometimes God puts us in situations where we stand before what we cannot bear, so that we stop relying on ourselves and turn to rely on the power of Christ.

So do not be afraid to admit weakness. Recognizing our weakness is not despair, but the door that leads us to find grace. When our strength is exhausted, we can find the Savior who is strong and full of mercy.

Father, all-powerful God, I praise you because you show kindness to the weak and are my true strength. Please forgive me when I hide my weakness and rely on my own strength.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who came to me in my weakness and gave me sufficient grace, that the Holy Spirit would humble me, acknowledge my weakness, and rely on His power. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ today. Amen.

title: The mercy is not only to pardon but to give strength.
body:
The blessings of the gospel are not limited to forgiveness of sins and receiving us alone. The same blessings also lift us up and give us strength to live out the calling of God in our lives today.

We often fear when God calls us to obey. We feel that we are weak, not ready, and unable to do it. But God does not call us and then leave us to rely on our own resources alone.

God did not tell us to wait until we see the full power before we obey, but He calls us to step out in faith because He is with us, for us, and is working in us by the Holy Spirit.

The power of God is a power that encompasses the entire world. This great God knows His children and gives them the necessary blessings at the necessary time. Therefore, rise up today and follow Him by relying on His grace.

Our faithful and powerful Father, I praise you, for you not only forgive my sins, but also give me the strength to obey. Forgive me when I look at my own inadequacies more than at your promises.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who has helped me to be saved and has given me the Holy Spirit to dwell in me. May I walk by faith, not by fear, and obey Him in what He is calling me to do today. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Hope Has Come
body:
We often think that hope comes when circumstances change, when problems are solved, or when we see clear evidence that everything will get better. But the hope that the Bible teaches does not begin with our surroundings.

The true hope is one person, and His name is Jesus Christ. Jesus came to this world, faced what we face, and overcame what destroys us, to save us from destruction.

Those who are in Christ are not hopeless. Our problems are not a lack of hope, but rather not seeing the hope that God has given us. We may not see the inheritance and the great power that we have received in Christ.

Therefore, we must ask God to open the eyes of our hearts, and when the Holy Spirit opens our eyes to see the gospel, we will find that even in today's suffering, hope in Christ is a true and sufficient hope.

Our Father, our hope, we praise you because you give us a firm hope in Jesus Christ. Forgive us when we look at the present situation and live like people without hope.

I thank Jesus Christ, the true hope of my soul, that the Holy Spirit may open my eyes to see the inheritance, the blessings, and the power that are in Christ, and that I may live in hope today, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Think of things above.
body:
Humans always look at life from a certain perspective. Our thoughts are never neutral. What we believe about God, ourselves, and the purpose of life will influence our words, decisions, and actions. The Bible speaks of two ways to think: worldly thinking and heavenly-mindedness. If we focus on the world alone, desires, success, fear, and what can be seen today seem like everything in life.

But those who are new with Christ are called to seek the things that are above. This does not mean we deny the realities of daily life, but it means we view everything through a larger story, namely the gospel of Jesus Christ.

Today our schedules, decisions, relationships, and priorities are driven by what? God does not allow our thoughts to be bound up with this world but changes us so that we look at life from Christ's perspective who is Lord over all.

Father who is true, I praise you because you have changed my thoughts and direction of life in Jesus Christ. Please forgive me when I look to the world and live according to fear or self-will.

Thank you that He gave new life in Christ who rose from death. May the Holy Spirit take control of my thoughts, may I think about things above, and choose to live according to good news today. Pray in Jesus' name Amen.

title: Sins often do not appear as sins.
body:
The terrifying deception of sin is that when we commit sin, sin often does not appear to be sin. It often makes itself appear small, ordinary, and reasonable, so we may overlook its ugliness and destructive power.

The Bible does not hide the severity of sin and wickedness. Sin destroys humanity, corrupts the life that God has given, and separates us from God. Sin is not a game and is not a small matter.

But the Bible does not only talk about the fear of sin, no matter how great it is, and how powerful it may seem. The grace of salvation of Jesus Christ is greater. We should hate sin seriously, but not despair like a defeated person.

Christ has conquered sin and death, so we should not play with sin, but we also should not be afraid that sin has power over our Savior. In His grace, we have true hope.

Father, holy and pure, I pray that you will help me. I praise you because you have revealed to me the severity of sin and have delivered me from sin in Christ. Please forgive me when I view sin as a small thing and excuse my own desires.

Thank God for Jesus Christ, the One who has conquered sin and death. May the Holy Spirit give us a heart that hates sin, and at the same time, a firm faith in the goodness of God, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: When Longing Becomes Necessity
body:
We often turn what we want into what we think we need. At first, it may be just a desire, but as we begin to feel that we cannot live without it, that desire starts to occupy our hearts.

When desire becomes necessity, we begin to demand from God. We might think that God must give me this, and we start to judge God's love or faithfulness by whether He gives us that thing or not.

But God never promised to give us everything we want. He is a Father who knows what is truly necessary for us, because we often confuse our desires with our needs. We need His wisdom and His grace.

Jesus came to set us free from worshiping idols in our hearts. The good news frees the heart that has been bound by desire and teaches us to trust the Father who knows and prepares what we truly need.

Our Father, all-knowing God, I praise you because you know what is truly necessary for me and have prepared it with your goodness. Please forgive me when I call my own desires necessary and doubt your love when I do not get what I want.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who has set me free from the slavery of desire. May the Holy Spirit transform my heart to trust in the wisdom of the Father more than my own desires. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: God is the Center, Not Us
body:
The center of the universe is not us, but God. He is the one who fills heaven and earth, and He is the one who determines what is love, wisdom, righteousness, and grace. All things come from Him, through Him, and for Him.

But sin makes us want to sit in God's place, we want our lives to go according to our desires, to have our plans succeed, and for those around us to adjust to us. This leads to strained relationships and disappointment in the heart.

Selfishness is a major work of sin. The more we try to be the center, the less we love God and our neighbors correctly. Therefore, we need the grace that saves us.

In Jesus Christ, grace brings us back to the right place, where God is at the center, and we are the ones created to worship and depend on Him. When we acknowledge this truth, our lives begin to return to their proper order.

Our Father, who is the center of all things, I praise you, for you are worthy of all glory, power, and praise. Please forgive me when I want my life to revolve around my own desires and plans.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who has led me back to worship in the right way. May the Holy Spirit humble my heart and live my life centered on God today. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: We Need a Community of Love
body:
Life in a world fallen into sin is not easy. For this reason, God did not design the Christian life for us to walk alone. We are called to be one body in Jesus and are established to be instruments of grace to one another.

But we often think that the church is just a place we attend or a certain religious activity. We don't want anyone to know us too deeply, so we keep up a good image and keep our relationships at a safe distance.

But what is not revealed cannot be helped. God uses a community centered on Christ to warn us, protect us, comfort us, and bring us back to Him.

The church community is therefore not a minor option, but a spiritual necessity. The love and grace of Jesus are manifested in our lives through His body, which is the church.

Father, who is love, I praise you because you called me into the body of Christ and gave me the benefit through your community. Please forgive me when I think I can live the spiritual life on my own or refuse to open up in relationships.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who has made me a part of His body. May the Holy Spirit open my heart to receive and share the blessings in the community of prayer in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Our identity is not from success.
body:
We often try to prove who we are through our work, achievements, and the approval of others. We work hard to find meaning, purpose, peace, and admiration, and wait for someone to affirm our worth.

But in Christ, we no longer have to search for our identity. The goodness of God connects us to Him, and God calls us His children.

We do not work to gain identity, but work with gratitude in the identity that God has given us. Our value is not based on success, but on the grace received in Christ.

Thus, failure does not have to destroy us, and success does not have to make us proud. In Christ, we are already children of God; this is a more stable truth than what we can or cannot do.

Our Father, who has accepted us as your children, I praise you because you have given us your true self in Jesus Christ. Please forgive me when I try to prove my worth by my achievements or the approval of others.

We thank You that You have called us to be Your children in Christ. May the Holy Spirit establish our hearts in Your grace, and may we work, serve, and live with gratitude, not out of fear of being worthless, praying in the name of Jesus Christ, Amen.

title: Wisdom comes from a relationship with Christ.
body:
Sin makes us foolish; we often think we are wise enough to manage our own lives and interpret life according to our desires, experiences, or the standards of the world, but the heart of the sinner is more crooked than we think.

Wisdom that is genuine does not come from many experiences or learning alone, because even our experiences and knowledge are still interpreted through an imperfect heart. We need to be rescued from ourselves first.

Wisdom is the result of relationship. Jesus Christ has the treasure of all wisdom and knowledge hidden in His grace, leading us to have a relationship with Him, who is our wisdom.

Right now, the all-wise Lord is leading us, warning us, teaching us, comforting us, and changing our desires to new thoughts. Today, we should seek wisdom from Him with humble and grateful hearts.

Dear Heavenly Father, I praise You, for You have placed the treasure of wisdom and knowledge in all things in Jesus Christ. Please forgive me when I rely on my own experiences, thoughts, and standards more than on You.

Thank God, the Christ, who is my wisdom, may the Holy Spirit humble me, seek wisdom from above, and lead me according to His guidance today. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: We are created to depend on God.
body:
We often find it difficult to ask for help. We do not want to say that we do not know, we do not want to admit that we are weak, and we want others to see that we can get by on our own. This is not just a matter of personality, but something that sin does in our hearts.

Sin sows the idea of independence in our hearts, deceiving us that we do not need to rely on God and do not need to rely on one another. It makes us think that we have wisdom, power, and righteousness in ourselves more than the truth.

We were not created to be self-sufficient, but to rely on God. The dream of being self-sufficient is not freedom, but a nightmare. A life that tries to be sufficient without God will result in unrighteousness, falsehood, and death.

The kindness of Jesus Christ frees us from the illusion of independence. He brings us back into a relationship with God who has everything we truly need.

Our Father, the Creator, I praise you because you created me to rely on you, and in Christ you have brought me back to you again. Please forgive me when I act like myself and do not want your favor.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who has helped me to be free from self-reliance. May the Holy Spirit humble me and teach me to rely on God, and receive help through the instrument of God's grace, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Being counted as righteous is the foundation of transformation.
body:
God's acceptance of us is not based on our self-improvement, but rather He declares us righteous by His grace. This is the foundation of the transformation in our lives. Spiritual change does not make us righteous, but being declared righteous is what leads to change.

We did not reform our lives first and then come to God, but God gave us His Son first, redeemed us, made us His people, and cleansed us. The beginning of all this was not our intention, but the powerful grace of God.

This grace teaches us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires and to live a self-controlled, godly life in the present age, looking forward to the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us to redeem us from all wickedness and to purify for himself a people for his own possession who are zealous for good deeds. Therefore, do not throw away your confidence, which has a great reward. For you have need of endurance, so that when you have done the will of God you may receive the promise.

If Jesus Christ had not given Himself for us, we would not be able to have a relationship with God and would not be able to have new life. The most valuable thing in the Christian life is not something we have acquired on our own, but a gift of grace that truly changes us.

Our Father, who counts sinners as righteous in Christ, I praise you because you have accepted me and changed my life through your kindness. Please forgive me when I try to use my own goodness or self-improvement as the basis for approaching you.

I thank Jesus Christ, who has given himself for me, and has made me righteous by His grace. May the Holy Spirit transform my life further, that I may bear fruit of His grace. Not to try to reason why He loves me, but to pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: The Grace Reveals Our Sinfulness to Us
body:
Sin blinds our spiritual eyes. We often think of ourselves as being better and more righteous than we actually are, so we see the sins of others more clearly than our own sins.

Like the church in Laodicea, we may think we are rich and have everything we need, but in the sight of God, our true condition may be poor, blind, and naked. Sin deceives us, and we often cooperate with that deception without realizing it.

The true spiritual sight does not make us judge others more, but makes us sorrowful over our own sins and repent. If we are more awakened to the sins of others than to our own, that is a significant warning sign.

So we must ask for a rebuke full of grace from the Holy Spirit. When He opens our eyes, we will not be pushed into despair, but will be brought back to Jesus Christ through repentance and faith.

Father, our Lord, I praise you because you have opened my eyes to see my own sin through the Holy Spirit. Please forgive me when I trust in my own righteousness and am more concerned with the sins of others than my own.

We thank Jesus Christ, who redeems sinners by His grace. May the Holy Spirit convict and awaken us to repent of our own sins, turn to Him sincerely, and come to Christ in prayer with hope in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: In Suffering, We Are Not Alone
body:
The Bible does not deny the suffering of this world and does not minimize the pain. The Bible speaks the truth about the difficulties of life, but at the same time, it gives us hope.

Like the prayer in the Psalms, the people of God cry out to Him in the midst of suffering. Sometimes it seems as though God is silent, and the prosperity of the wicked may cause our hearts to waver, but the prayer of the believer does not end in despair.

Our God is the strength and shield of His people, a refuge in times of distress. When our hearts trust in Him, we receive help and are able to praise Him again.

God's grace leads us into suffering and waiting, but He never calls us to stand alone by His own power. The Savior, who is the Refuge of salvation, is always with us.

Our Father, the Refuge, I praise You because You do not leave Your people to suffer alone. Please forgive me when I forget that You are with me and try to endure by my own strength.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, the Savior of my soul. May the Holy Spirit sustain my heart to cry out to Him in my troubles and to receive comfort from Him again. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Comfort that is received should flow to others.
body:
When we see someone who is suffering, we may respond with judgment rather than comfort. We may look at their weakness and quickly assess what they did wrong, or why they ended up in that condition. This is a result of the self-righteousness that still remains in our hearts.

Sometimes God leads us into difficult situations that reveal our weakness and foolishness. He does not do this to destroy us, but to humble us and to give us compassionate hearts towards others who are suffering.

God is the God of all comfort. He comforts us in our affliction so that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction with the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God. Our affliction is not just for our growth, but also to make us a means of God's comfort to others.

The comfort we receive in Christ is not given to us alone. The Father, who sees not, causes His comfort to be revealed through our words, our listening, and our service.

Our Father, the God of comfort, I praise you because you have comforted me in my affliction and called me to share that comfort with others. Forgive me when I judge those who are hurting more than I love and encourage them.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who is merciful and comforting to me. May the Holy Spirit make my heart tender, so that today I may pass on the mercy and comfort of Him to those who pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: The Mercy Changes the Heart
body:
The grace of God does not stop at making us do things differently. His grace transforms us at the deepest level of our hearts, making us truly new people.

In Psalm 51, David did not pray only for God to help him change his behavior, but he prayed for God to create a clean heart in him. The problem of sin is not just in the environment or external actions, but it starts from the heart.

We do not want a better situation, but a new heart. For we are sinners who cannot create a new heart for ourselves. A new heart is something that only God can create.

Jesus Christ did not die just to improve our outward appearance. He gave Himself to us so that we might receive a new heart, and to continually change that heart by His grace.

Dear Heavenly Father, I praise You because You have changed my heart to Jesus Christ. Please forgive me when I try to fix things on the outside, but refuse to deal with the sin in my heart seriously.

I thank Jesus Christ, who gave me new life through the cross and resurrection. May the Holy Spirit deeply change my heart, so that I may truly love and obey Him. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: The way of God is better than our way.
body:
We often feel that our plan is better than God’s will. If we let go of the difficulties now, we are still happier. Or if we choose another way. Life is still better than this, but our eyes see only a short moment, God sees our whole life and eternity.

Sometimes getting out of a difficult situation may seem to be the wisest option, but over time we may see that God has used that difficulty to train our faith and entice us to grow even more. Even when we think it’s a failure, God can use it as an instrument of charity.

Our life is not a story that flows by chance. God planned all our days with wisdom and love. Even the ways we don’t understand, the times to wait long and the moments filled with tears are under His good will.

Above all, God has done the best for us, and He has given His only Son, Jesus Christ, to take our sins on the threshold, and to give us eternal life by being from death. God, who does not worship His Son, will lead our lives in the best way.

Prayer: The wise and loving Father, I praise You, for You have always guided Your Son in the best way. Please forgive me when I trust my thoughts and plans more than your wishes.

May the Holy Spirit give me faith, trust in God’s plan even in unknown circumstances, and be happy to follow Him today. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ Amen.

title: The Lord's way is better than our way.
body:
We often feel that our plans are better than God's will. If we could escape from our present difficulties, we would be much happier, or if we could choose another path, our lives would be better. But our eyes can see only a short period of time, while God sees our entire lives and eternity.

Sometimes leaving a difficult situation may seem like the wisest choice, but as time passes, we may see that God used that hardship to train our faith and shape us to grow even more, and even in the periods we considered to be failures, God can use them as instruments of His grace.

Our lives are not a story that unfolds by chance. God has planned all our days with wisdom and love. Even the paths we do not understand, the times of lengthy waiting, and the seasons filled with tears are under His good providence.

Above all, God has done the greatest thing for us. He gave us His only Son, Jesus Christ, to bear our sins on the cross and to give us eternal life by raising Him from the dead. God, who did not withhold His Son, will also lead us in the best way.

Dear Father, all-wise and full of love, I praise you because you always lead your children in the best way. Please forgive me when I trust in my own thoughts and plans more than your will.

I thank You for giving me Jesus Christ to help me be saved. May the Holy Spirit give me faith. Trust in God's plan even in situations that are not yet understood. Rejoice in following You today. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Complaining to Praise
body:
Each day, we can find reasons to complain, and we can also find reasons to be thankful. The attitude we use to live our lives does not depend solely on our circumstances, but depends on where our hearts are turned.

Complaining begins when we place ourselves at the center of our lives. When our desires are not fulfilled, our expectations are not met, or our feelings are hurt, we often become angry and complain. Sin causes us to think that we deserve certain things and makes us blind to the many blessings that God has already given us.

But the good news turns our eyes away from ourselves to God. Before God, we have nothing to boast about, but He has shown us great mercy by giving us Jesus Christ, His only Son, to forgive our sins and receive us as His children.

Gratitude is not an emotion that arises only when circumstances improve, but it is the result of a life that acknowledges the grace of God. The more we look to the cross, the less we complain, and gratitude and praise grow.

Our Father, full of mercy and kindness, I praise you because you have given me many good things, even though I do not deserve them. Especially, I thank you for the gift of salvation through Jesus Christ. Please forgive me when I complain easily and forget the blessings I have received.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who made sinners children of God. May the Holy Spirit change my heart to remember the gift of the cross and praise Him with thanksgiving and praise in every situation, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: God Provides for Those He Calls
body:
God calls us to do things that we cannot do in our own strength. Noah could not put all the animals into the ark by himself. Moses could not lead the Israelites out of Egypt by his own power, and David could not defeat Goliath by his own strength.

But God called them, and He provided everything they needed. The Scripture does not teach that the people of God are strong enough to do God's work by themselves, but it teaches that God uses the weak and gives them the necessary grace and strength.

Our lives are the same, we cannot love others as Jesus loves us by our own strength. We cannot keep our hearts pure by ourselves, but God gives the Holy Spirit to believers and gives everything necessary for life and faith.

So when God calls us to obey, do not look at your own weakness, but look to Jesus Christ, who is our strength. Today we can walk by faith because God who calls us will always give us strength.

Dear Father, all-powerful and full of mercy, I praise you because you call the weak and provide all that is necessary for your children. Please forgive me when I look only at my own weakness and forget to trust in your power.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who has helped me to be saved and has given me the Holy Spirit to dwell in me. Please help me not to rely on my own strength, but on Your mercy, and walk in the path that You call me to, by praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: The Father does not break the bruised reed.
body:
Sometimes we may feel lonely, weary, and as if no one understands our hearts. We may feel that our wounds are invisible and that no one cares, but the children of God are never truly alone, for the Father is always with us in love.

Isaiah 42:3 says that He will not break the bruised reed, nor quench the smoking flax. This picture shows us the tender heart of God. Man may quickly judge the weak or make the suffering feel worse, but the Father is not like that.

God has clearly revealed this love in Jesus Christ. Jesus knows our weakness, He is the Savior who is full of mercy and restores the broken sinner. When we are weak, He does not mock us. When we are discouraged, He does not abandon us.

Therefore, if loneliness and despair enter your heart today, remember the gentle and faithful love of the Father. Although others may not understand us, in Jesus Christ, we are never forsaken.

Dear Father, full of mercy and love, I praise You. You do not break the bruised reed, nor quench the smoking flax. Please forgive me when I forget Your love and get stuck in my own isolation.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who knows my weakness and helps me to be a child of God. Please let the Holy Spirit comfort me and help me to trust in the sincere love of the Father, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: God Prepares
body:
We are living between what God has already accomplished and what still awaits fulfillment. Jesus Christ has died and been raised from the dead to save us, and the Holy Spirit already dwells in believers, but the struggle against sin is not yet over.

In our hearts, there is always a spiritual war going on, a war between faith and doubt, between obedience and rebellion, between worry and trust, and the crucial question that often arises is, will God really provide for us?

When we encounter difficulties or see our own weaknesses, we may fear that we are not enough. We may doubt whether we have sufficient strength, whether we have enough of what is necessary, and whether God is truly with us.

But God reminds us that He has not abandoned His people. He has given us Jesus Christ, the greatest gift of all. So we can trust that He will give us the blessings we need for today.

Our faithful Father, who provides for all things, I praise you, because you do not abandon your children and give us what we need at the right time. Please forgive me when I look at my weakness more than your promise.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who has helped me to be saved, and thank you that the Holy Spirit dwells in me. Please help me to believe that the greatest Giver of blessings will also give me the necessary blessings for today, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: In Christ, We Do Not Fear
body:
Deep down in the heart of humanity, there is always fear. We fear that we will not be loved. We fear that if others really knew us, they might not accept us. And we fear that we will not have what is necessary for life.

But God has clearly answered these fears. God loves those who do not deserve love. He did not love us with words only, but He has demonstrated His love by giving us Jesus Christ, His Son, to save us. In Christ, we are fully accepted and become children of God.

God's mercy is a complete forgiveness. Righteous Jesus died on the cross in place of sinners. Therefore, those who are in Christ are no longer under God's judgment. It is not because our sins are overlooked, but because Jesus has borne our sins in reality.

God's blessings are a matter of complete preparation. The Creator and Sustainer of all things always provides the necessary blessings to His children. Therefore, believers do not have to live in fear because in Jesus Christ, we receive love, are forgiven, and receive the necessary blessings for life.

Dear heavenly Father, who loves, forgives, and provides everything, I praise you, because in Jesus Christ, you have accepted sinners as your children. Please forgive me when I forget your mercies and let fear take over my heart.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who bore our sins on the cross and rose from the dead to give us new life. Please let the Holy Spirit make my heart firm in the love of forgiveness and pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Don't Hide, Come to the Lord
body:
When our sin is exposed, the first thing we often want to do is hide. We may make excuses, shift the blame to others, or tell ourselves that what we did was not that serious. But this kind of response usually comes from fear. We fear being rejected, being rebuked, or being punished.

But God's kindness calls us to come to Him with hope, not with fear. Jesus Christ bore our guilt, He bore our shame, and He bore God's wrath on the cross. Therefore, those who are in Christ do not need to hide their sins.

This does not mean that sin is a small thing, but that our Savior is greater than our sin. When we cover up, excuse, or shift the blame to others, we are forgetting the truth of God's grace. God's grace does not deceive us, but makes us bold to be honest with God.

Because of this, when the Holy Spirit makes us see our sin, do not flee, do not deny, and do not excuse, but come to Jesus Christ with a humble heart, because in Him there is sufficient forgiveness and restoration for the sinner always.

Dear Holy and merciful Father, I praise you because you have opened the way of forgiveness and restoration through Jesus Christ. Please forgive me when I see my own sin and hide, excuse, or shift the blame to others.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who bore my guilt and shame on the cross. Please let the Holy Spirit make me hate sin, and at the same time, I am confident in His goodness, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: The favor of God makes us not to pretend.
body:
The heart that is trapped in sin often wants others to see us as better than we really are. We want to appear smarter, stronger, and more righteous than we actually are. So, sometimes we hide our weakness, conceal our sin, and pretend that we don't need help.

But God's favor is not called us to a fake life. God does not accept us because of the image we create for ourselves, but because of what Jesus Christ has done for us. We are saved by His grace, not by our own actions. Therefore, we have nothing to boast about and do not need to pretend to be someone we are not.

God gives us what we do not seek, and He forgives our sins in truth. Therefore, God makes us bold to be honest. We no longer have to create our identity from our achievements or from the opinions of others. Our true identity is in Christ; we are children of God by His grace.

So, today, do not try to protect yourself with a false image. Admit your weakness, confess your sins, and ask for help. For in Jesus Christ, God knows us truly, forgives us completely, and loves us steadfastly.

Dear Father, who is true and full of mercy, I praise you, because in Jesus Christ you know me truly and still love and forgive me. Please forgive me when I want to be better than I am, when I hide my weakness and try to boast in things that are not from me.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who died in our place and granted us the righteousness that we could not attain on our own. May the Holy Spirit free our hearts from hypocrisy and help us live with sincerity, humility, and trust in Your grace. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ, Amen.

title: The Mercy Leads Us Back to Worship
body:
Fish were created to swim, the sun was created to shine, and humans were created to worship our living God. Our lives were not created for ourselves, but to know God, to love God, and to glorify Him.

But sin has stolen our worship away, and the heart that should be given to God turns to the things God has made. We begin to seek life, satisfaction, and meaning in other things instead of God. This is the greatest damage of sin.

The grace of God does not only make us better people, but it also brings us back to the original purpose for which God created us, which is to worship Him. Grace changes the direction of our hearts and brings God back to the rightful place in our lives.

Jesus Christ died on the cross and rose from the dead, not only to forgive our sins, but to restore us to worship God. In Christ, we can call God our Father and offer Him honor with our hearts and lives.

Our Father, worthy of all glory and praise, I praise you because you created me to know and worship you. Forgive me when I love the things you have made more than you, and seek satisfaction in something other than God.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who died and rose from the dead to forgive sins and bring me back to the Father. Please have the Holy Spirit turn my heart back to You, and help my life be a worship that glorifies God in every prayer I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Those who receive blessings are called to be instruments of blessings.
body:
The blessings of Jesus Christ are not only for salvation, but also to make us instruments of His blessings. God helps His people to be saved and uses them to spread the good news to others.

The great commission that Jesus gave to the disciples is the commission given to the church as a whole. The work of proclaiming the gospel and making disciples is not the task of just a few people, but God calls every believer to manifest the power of Christ in the place where He has placed him.

We often separate our lives from our service, but those whom Christ has redeemed with His blood no longer own their own lives. Our time, relationships, words, service, and daily lives all belong to the Lord.

This is not a heavy burden first, but a great honor. God uses weak people like us as instruments in the work of redemption. Grace not only saves us, but also calls us to participate in God's earthly work.

Our Father, help us. We praise you, because in Jesus Christ, you not only saved us, but also called us to be part of the work of redemption. Forgive us when we live as if we are our own, and think that the work of the gospel is the task of some people only.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who bought me with His blood. Please let the Holy Spirit change my heart to remember that my whole life belongs to You. May my words, service, and relationships declare the goodness of Christ. Pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

title: Leaving Your Own Small Kingdom
body:
The grace of God is not only forgiveness of our sins, but also life for something greater than ourselves. We may think that spiritual life is doing religious activities such as reading the Bible, worshiping, giving, or participating in service work. But even if we do these things, we may still be living for our own small kingdom.

True Christian living is not just about what we do, but about whose our hearts are. Outwardly, we may appear to be serving God, but inwardly, we may be seeking the approval of others, our own self-satisfaction, or our own glory. We may talk about God's kingdom, but in reality, our own needs and plans may still be at the center.

The problem of the Pharisees was this: they had many religious activities, but their hearts were not truly surrendered to God. Outwardly they appeared clean, but inwardly they were full of greed and selfishness. True righteousness does not come from an outward appearance, but from a heart that has been transformed by grace.

So we should not go back to living for our own small kingdoms. Jesus Christ has rescued us from sin and self-centeredness, and He calls us to live for God's kingdom. His kindness makes our hearts submit to God, and our lives have a greater and more beautiful purpose than before.

Holy and glorious Father, I praise you, for you not only forgive my sins, but also call me to live for your glory. Forgive me when I serve you with my hands, but in my heart I seek my own glory, satisfaction, and desires.

Thank you, Jesus Christ, who died and rose from the dead to help me out of sin and self-centeredness. Please let the Holy Spirit take control of my heart, so that my life will no longer be my own, but will be for You, praying in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
